public_rationale: Zitron hedged: nobody 'appears' to have built an AI-services business that actually makes a profit. As of the June 2, 2026 post, the record fits that. Anthropic's S-1 shows an $8.06 billion operating loss for 2025. OpenAI's shareholder documents show a $9.3 billion operating loss in Q1 2026. CoreWeave, the largest GPU cloud, also reported a Q1 2026 loss. Anthropic's first profit was only a forecast to investors in May. Later, Anthropic reported a $974 million GAAP operating profit for Q2 2026 and an adjusted profit for the half. That quarter ended after the post, and the first half still showed a GAAP operating loss and an $80.7 billion net loss. So it weakens the claim going forward but does not make it false when made.
limitations: Only the largest pure-play AI-services providers were checked. 'Nobody' cannot be fully confirmed.
Diversified profitable firms selling AI products are excluded because they do not report AI profit separately. Including them could change the result.
Anthropic's Q2 2026 profit covers a quarter that started before the post.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Nobody appears to have built a profitable business model for AI services, despite unlimited capital and the tech industry's full focus.

statement.excerpt: There’s a cost to having them sit idle — both in electricity and personnel — and unless the plan is to have them sit in a data center turned off until you can find somebody else to sell them to, you’ll have to come up with a business model for your AI services that actually makes a profit…which nobody appears to have done, even with unlimited capital and the entire focus of the tech industry.

from_speaker: you'll have to come up with a business model for your AI services that actually makes a profit
which nobody appears to have done
even with unlimited capital and the entire focus of the tech industry
our_interpretation: The hedge 'appears' is respected. The claim is about the visible record as of the post: whether any company selling AI services (model labs, GPU clouds) had publicly shown a business that actually makes a profit.
'Actually makes a profit' is read as profit under standard reporting (GAAP operating or net income), not adjusted figures that exclude costs such as stock-based compensation.

Target period: from the start of 2025 to the post date (2026-06-02). This is the record the speaker could see when he wrote 'appears to have done'. Later-reported results for quarters ending after the post are context.
The claim is mainly about firms running AI data centers or selling AI model services. Diversified companies whose AI results are not reported separately, such as hyperscalers, are not counted.
criteria.support_condition: Would be supported if, as of the post, the main AI service providers with public figures all showed losses over the recent periods and none had shown an actually profitable AI-services business.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Would be contradicted if, as of the post, a significant AI-services company had reported real (GAAP) profit from its AI services in a recent period.

evidence.explanation: Per its S-1, Anthropic, a leading AI-model seller, lost $8.06 billion at the operating level in 2025. That fits the claim that no AI-services business had shown it was profitable.

evidence.explanation: Counterevidence. Anthropic had a GAAP operating profit in Q2 2026, but that quarter ended after the post and the first half still showed an operating loss and a large net loss. It shows the situation changed soon after the post.
